jsonld.description: Generative engine optimisation for D2C, B2B and education brands: entity clarity, source quality and citations so generative AI tools describe and cite the brand accurately.

acceptedAnswer.text: Generative engine optimisation is the work of making your brand a clear, consistent and citable source for generative AI tools such as ChatGPT, Perplexity, Gemini and Google AI Overviews, so they describe and cite you accurately.

mainEntity.name: How is GEO different from SEO?

acceptedAnswer.text: SEO aims to rank pages in search results. GEO aims to influence how generative tools describe and cite your brand, which depends more on entity clarity, source quality and third-party mentions than on a single page's ranking.

mainEntity.name: How is GEO different from AEO?

acceptedAnswer.text: AEO shapes pages into short answers for snippets and voice. GEO works on whether generative tools know who you are, trust your sources and cite you. We run both inside AI SEO.

mainEntity.name: Can you get us into ChatGPT answers?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Nobody outside an AI or search company can promise a citation, a ranking or a position in an answer, and the systems change often. We commit to the work in the monthly scope and to reporting what we can observe.

mainEntity.name: Do we need an llms.txt file?

acceptedAnswer.text: It is a proposed convention, and tools differ in whether they read it. It is cheap to provide and harmless, so we usually add one alongside the work that matters more: clear pages, consistent facts and credible sources.

A monthly scope, agreed after a call and written down so you can see what each month covers. We do not publish a price list because the right scope depends on your site, your market and how much you want done.

Brands that buyers ask AI about. We do this for D2C, B2B and education brands and set it up differently for each: D2C on products and repeat purchase, B2B on specifications and enquiries, education on courses and admissions.

hub.sub: Generative tools build answers from sources they trust. We make your brand a clear, consistent, citable source.

answer.label: In short
answer.lead: Generative engine optimisation (GEO) is the work of becoming a source that ChatGPT, Perplexity, Gemini and Google AI Overviews draw on and cite when they answer buyers. It rests on clear entity facts, quotable original content, trusted third-party mentions and pages that AI crawlers can read.
answer.hl: a source that generative tools draw on and cite
answer.who: Monday Marketing Company (MMC) does GEO for D2C, B2B and education brands, as one workstream inside our AI SEO programme.

answer.chip: Cited by the tools buyers ask

blocks.h: How generative tools choose what to cite
paras: Generative tools combine what they learned in training with sources fetched at answer time. Which sources they favour is not published and differs by tool, so no one can honestly promise a result.

What does hold across them is simple: a brand that is easy to identify, described consistently by credible sources and backed by specific, useful pages is easier to cite correctly than one that is vague or contradictory.

leaks.lede: Each stage below is where a brand fails to be cited or is described wrongly, and the GEO work that corrects it.

stages.k: Check what AI says about you
stages.breaks: Never asking the tools about your own brand.
stages.why: Assistants can omit you, confuse you with another firm or repeat outdated facts.
stages.does: We ask a fixed set of category and brand questions across the main tools and record what is said, cited and wrong.

stages.breaks: Different names, descriptions and facts in different places.
stages.why: Contradictions make it harder for a system to be sure which brand a fact belongs to.
stages.does: We align your name, offer, locations and key facts on your site, profiles and listings, and mark them up.

stages.breaks: Generic pages that say what every competitor says.
stages.why: A tool has little reason to cite a page that adds nothing new.
stages.does: We build pages with your own specifics: methods, comparisons, definitions, data you hold and are allowed to share.

stages.breaks: Relying only on your own website.
stages.why: Reviews, directories, publications and community sources help confirm who you are.
stages.does: We work on reviews, listings and relevant media so credible sources describe you consistently. No paid link schemes.

stages.k: Let AI crawlers in, on your terms
stages.breaks: Blocking or ignoring AI crawlers by accident.
stages.why: Robots rules and rendering can stop AI tools reading your pages, or allow more than you intended.
stages.does: We review crawler access, rendering and an llms.txt file, and set a policy you choose deliberately.
